text:
maya: Heads-up — onboarding/sampleapp: logs missing request IDs when OTEL auto-instrumentation is enabled. Local repro: header present on incoming req, but loghook prints `reqId: -`. Not sure if redact or hook ordering. :thinking:

sam: Can you paste the middleware order from the sample app? quick guess: req-id middleware is running after the otel/express instrumentation so the log hook never sees it.

maya: Repro snippet:
```js
// index.js (simplified)
const app = express();
app.use(opentelemetry.middleware()); // auto-instrumentation shim
app.use(require('request-id-middleware')());
app.use(require('./loghook')());
app.get('/health', (req, res) => res.send('ok'));
```
In this order, req.id exists on req but logs still show `-`. If I move request-id middleware before OTEL middleware it works locally.

evans: :facepalm: that's the classic ordering bug. OTEL instrumentation can replace the request object or wrap the handler such that the log hook's sampling/context extract sees a different lifecycle. Moving req-id earlier is fine but not great for onboarding docs.

evans: Two options:
1) Make our loghook resolve req id from either `req.id` or `res.getHeader('x-request-id')` as a fallback.
2) Add an OTEL hook in the SDK that reads request attributes and populates our log context before the redactpass runs.

maya: Option 1 is the fastest patch. Option 2 is nicer long-term (so private deployment/auto-instrumentation doesn't break DX).

sam: Agree. Quick patch idea (fallback):
```js
function getReqId(req, res) {
  return req.id || req.headers['x-request-id'] || res.getHeader('x-request-id') || '-';
}
```
That should cover most cases.

devex: Also double-check our redaction pipeline. If the redact filter runs on headers before the loghook reads them we might strip header value entirely. We had a previous change that aggressively scrubbed headers early for GDPR reasons.

maya: Right — when I enable REDACT_STRICT=true locally the header is blanked by the time loghook runs, even if req.id existed earlier. So ordering + redaction both in play.

evans: For REDACT_STRICT we should whitelist an allowlist: `x-request-id` must survive redaction for internal telemetry. We can hash it if necessary but not erase. That way we preserve linkability without leaking PII.

devex: Proposal:
- Patch loghook fallback to check res header if req.id missing (hotfix)
- Add redact config `REDACT_ALLOWLIST_HEADERS="x-request-id"` and wire it into the redact middleware (docs + tests)
- Longer term: add an init hook in our SDK that registers before OTEL auto-instrumentation (or document ordering in onboarding guide)

maya: I'll open a PR for the hotfix and add a repro test. Adding the allowlist to redact sounds good — will coordinate with security review.

ci-bot: maya opened PR #4821: "hotfix(loghook): fallback to x-request-id header when req.id missing" — CI queued. :white_check_mark:

sam: Thanks all. Also adding a short note to onboarding quickstart: "Install request-id middleware before auto-instrumentation or enable redact allowlist." Keeps the first-run experience smoother.

maya: Will add the note and link PR once CI passes. Thanks! :thumbsup:
